facts.text: The Second Punic War, which began in 218 BC, saw the Carthaginian general Hannibal cross the Alps and invade Italy.
The Great Pyramid of Giza was the world's tallest human-made structure for more than 3,700 years.
The 793 Viking raid on the monastery of Lindisfarne is often considered the beginning of the Viking Age.
The Battle of Verdun, fought in 1916, was the longest battle of the First World War.
Michelangelo sculpted two of his best-known works, the Pietà and David, before the age of 30.
The Mongol siege and sack of Baghdad took place in early 1258.
Yuri Gagarin's Vostok 1, the first human orbital spaceflight, took 108 minutes from launch to landing.
When the Bastille was stormed in 1789, the prison held only seven inmates.
The Minoan civilisation is often regarded as the first civilisation in Europe.
The Liverpool and Manchester Railway was the first inter-city railway in the world.
During the Berlin Blockade, American and British air forces landed in Berlin more than 200,000 times with food, fuel and other necessities.
Sikhs regard the Guru Granth Sahib, their central scripture, as the eleventh and eternally living Guru.
Napoleon was born on Corsica to a family of Italian origin, and moved to mainland France in 1779.
The Black Death, a bubonic plague pandemic, reached England in June 1348.
Gandhi's 1930 Salt March covered 387 kilometres, from Sabarmati Ashram to Dandi.
The first public readings of the Declaration of Independence took place on 8 July 1776, in Trenton, Easton and Philadelphia.
In the 1453 siege of Constantinople, Ottoman cannons fired massive cannonballs weighing 500 kilograms.
Abraham Lincoln was shot on 14 April 1865 while attending a play at Ford's Theatre in Washington.
Chandragupta Maurya was the founder and first emperor of the Maurya Empire, based in Magadha, present-day Bihar.
The D-Day landings in Normandy on 6 June 1944 were the largest seaborne invasion in history.
In 1674 Shivaji was formally crowned Chhatrapati of his realm at Raigad Fort.
On Bloody Sunday in 1905, guards fired on a peaceful procession of workers outside the tsar's Winter Palace.
At its height, the British Empire was the largest empire in history.
By July 1932, the US stock market had lost some 90% of its value from before the 1929 crash.
The Battle of Haldighati was fought in 1576 between Maharana Pratap's Mewar forces and Mughal forces led by Man Singh I of Amber.
Norman Borlaug, called the Father of the Green Revolution, received the Nobel Peace Prize in 1970.
Lehman Brothers filed for bankruptcy in September 2008 in a case involving more than 600 billion US dollars in assets.
The dot-com stock market bubble developed during the late 1990s and peaked on 10 March 2000.
In 27 BC the Roman Senate gave Octavian the new title of Augustus, marking him as the first Roman emperor.
Cleopatra's first language was Koine Greek. She is the only Ptolemaic ruler known to have learned Egyptian.
L'Anse aux Meadows is an archaeological site of a Norse settlement from about 1000 CE, first excavated in the 1960s.
The Battle of the Somme saw the first use of the tank, though the new technology proved unreliable.
With an improved telescope he built, Galileo observed the phases of Venus, lunar craters and Jupiter's four largest moons.
The Mongol Empire was the largest contiguous empire in history.
The Hubble Space Telescope is the only telescope designed to be maintained in space by astronauts.
The 1789 Women's March on Versailles began among market women in Paris who were rioting over the high price of bread.
Alexander the Great took the throne of Macedon at the age of 20, after his father was assassinated.
The Bessemer process was the first inexpensive industrial method for mass-producing steel from molten pig iron.
It was called a cold war because the two superpowers never fought each other directly, though they backed sides in proxy wars.
In 1604 Guru Arjan, the fifth Sikh Guru, placed a copy of the Adi Granth in the Golden Temple.
The Battle of Waterloo, fought in what is now Belgium on 18 June 1815, was Napoleon's last engagement.
The plague bacterium was discovered in 1894 by Alexandre Yersin during an epidemic in Hong Kong.
The Indian National Congress was founded in December 1885 and held its first session that year in Bombay.
The Saratoga campaign of 1777 persuaded France to enter the war as an American ally in 1778.
Suleiman the Magnificent broke with Ottoman tradition in 1534 by marrying Hürrem, a woman from his Imperial Harem.
The Battle of Gettysburg in 1863 was the bloodiest battle of the American Civil War, with over 50,000 combined casualties.
The Arthashastra, an ancient text on statecraft, had its first English translation published in 1915.
Germany's failure to destroy Britain's air defences was its first major defeat of the Second World War.
The first Peshwa, Moropant Pingle, was appointed by Shivaji to head his council of eight ministers.
The February Revolution was the first of two revolutions that took place in Russia in 1917.
The East India Company was a joint-stock company founded in 1600 and dissolved in 1874.
The 1930 Smoot–Hawley Tariff Act raised American tariffs on over 20,000 imported goods.
Udaipur, known as the city of lakes, was founded by Udai Singh II, a Rana of Mewar.
Operation Flood, launched in India in 1970, was the world's largest dairy development programme.
The Dodd–Frank Act, named for Senator Chris Dodd and Representative Barney Frank, was signed by President Obama in 2010.
Webvan, a dot-com grocery business, filed for bankruptcy in 2001 after three years of operation.
During Rome's third-century crisis, at least 26 people claimed the title of emperor, mostly prominent Roman generals.
Tutankhamun's tomb was discovered in 1922 by excavators led by Howard Carter and his patron, the Earl of Carnarvon.
Rollo, a Viking who became Count of Rouen, was the first ruler of Normandy in today's northern France.
The Armistice ending the fighting of the First World War came into force at 11 a.m. Paris time on 11 November 1918.
Leonardo da Vinci spent his last three years in France at the invitation of Francis I, and died there in 1519.
Kublai Khan became the first non-Han emperor to rule all of China proper.
Data from August 2012 showed that the Voyager 1 probe had entered interstellar space.
The Estates General that opened at Versailles in May 1789 was the first such meeting since 1614.
Athens was not the first Greek city-state with democracy. Several others adopted similar constitutions before it.
At their peak there were five million spinning mule spindles in Lancashire alone.
The largest share of Marshall Plan money, about 26% of the total, went to the United Kingdom.
Guru Gobind Singh, the tenth Sikh Guru, founded the Khalsa in 1699 and introduced the Five Ks, five articles of faith.
Napoleon's Continental System was a large-scale embargo against the British Empire, begun in 1806.
The term 'Black Death' was not used until the late 17th century.
The Rebellion of 1857 began on 10 May as a mutiny of sepoys of the East India Company's garrison in Meerut.
The Boston Tea Party, an act of protest, took place on 16 December 1773.
The Janissary Corps was abolished by Sultan Mahmud II in 1826.
The American Civil War began on 12 April 1861, when Confederate forces bombarded Fort Sumter in Charleston harbour.
Ashoka, the third ruler of the Maurya Empire, conquered Kalinga after a brutal war.
At Stalingrad the German 6th Army surrendered in February 1943, the first of Hitler's field armies to do so.
By Peshwa Bajirao I's death in 1740, the Maratha Empire was among the largest powers of the Indian subcontinent.
In 1998, eighty years after they were killed, the remains of the Romanovs were reburied in a state funeral in Saint Petersburg.
Hong Kong was handed over from the United Kingdom to China at midnight on 1 July 1997.
President Franklin D. Roosevelt signed the Social Security Act into law on 14 August 1935.
Mewar remained a princely state until it joined the Union of India in 1947.
During the Bengal famine of 1943, effective relief arrived after a record rice harvest that December.
US house prices peaked in early 2006, then declined and reached new lows in 2011.
In January 2003, AOL reported an annual loss of 99 billion dollars, then the largest ever for a corporation.
After the First Punic War, Carthage paid large reparations and Sicily became the first Roman province.
The pharaoh Akhenaten began his reign as Amenhotep IV and changed his name in his fifth year.
According to the Primary Chronicle, Rurik's relative Oleg conquered Kiev in 882 and established the state of Kievan Rus'.
Mustafa Kemal Atatürk rose to prominence as a commander at Gallipoli and later became the first president of Turkey.
Michelangelo was the first Western artist whose biography was published during his lifetime.
Genghis Khan was born with the name Temüjin. He formally took his famous title at an assembly in 1206.
Mir, which operated from 1986 to 2001, was the first modular space station and was assembled in orbit.
Before the Revolution, France's first two estates made up 2% of the population. The third estate was the remaining 98%.
Mycenaean Greece is named after Mycenae, its most prominent site. At the head of its society was a king called a wanax.
Exhibits at the Great Exhibition included the first public flush toilets, invented by George Jennings.
Estonia was the first Soviet republic to declare state sovereignty, on 16 November 1988.
Guru Arjan compiled hymns of earlier Gurus and other saints into the Adi Granth, the first edition of the Sikh scripture.
In December 1804 Napoleon crowned himself Emperor of the French.
The Great Plague of London of 1665 to 1666 killed an estimated 100,000 people, almost a quarter of the city's population.
India and Pakistan legally came into existence as self-governing countries at midnight on 14 to 15 August 1947.
The Ottoman Sultanate was formally abolished by the Grand National Assembly of Turkey on 1 November 1922.
